title: clinical-observational study for the evaluation of changes in nutritional requirements following major amputations using indirect calorimetry
summary:
Nutritional therapy for patients in intensive care setting has a significant role in the recovery process. Current guidelines for nutritional therapy in critically ill patients recommend the use of indirect calorimetry as the gold standard for determining caloric needs. Indirect calorimetry uses the inhaled and exhaled gases to estimate caloric requirements. The aforementioned guideline also refers to a formula to estimate caloric needs (24 kcal × kg body weight or adapted based on BMI), with the formula being the standard approach in clinical practice.

There is no available data regarding how caloric requirements under resting conditions change in patients who have undergone major amputation. In particular, there is a lack of evidence whether the aforementioned formula can still be applied using body weight in such cases.

To address this question, 50 patients undergoing elective major amputation will undergo indirect calorimetry both immediately prior to (t0) and three days following the amputation (t1), in order to determine their energy expenditure and caloric requirements. These measurements will be supplemented with the determination of nutritional status using a standardized questionnaire (t0), as well as the measurement of height (t0) and body weight (t0 and t1).

The data will be used to potentially adjust the formula for determining caloric needs, enabling the exclusion of calorimetry in daily intensive care routines for patients who have undergone major amputation.
conditions: Change in caloric requirements under resting conditions following major amputation.
